title: Comparison: State Executive vs Union Executive

blocks.content: The Governor is appointed by the President by warrant under his hand and seal, and holds office during the pleasure of the President.

rows: Article 123 (When Parliament is not in session)
Article 213 (When State Legislature is not in session)
Article 161 (Excludes Court-Martial and cannot pardon Death Sentences)

items: The Governor cannot pardon a death sentence even if it is prescribed under a state law; only the President holds the power to fully pardon death sentences.
There is no position of Vice-Governor at the State level, unlike the Vice-President at the Union level.
Articles to remember for ordinance power: Article 123 for the President and Article 213 for the Governor.
The Attorney General of India (Article 76) is part of the Union Executive, whereas the Advocate General for the State (Article 165) belongs to the State Executive.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Union Executive consists of the President, Vice-President, Prime Minister, Council of Ministers, and Attorney General of India.
The State Executive consists of the Governor, Chief Minister, Council of Ministers, and Advocate General of the State.
While the President is elected indirectly by an electoral college, the Governor is nominated by the Centre and appointed by the President.
The President has exclusive authority to pardon death sentences and military court-martial sentences under Article 72, which the Governor lacks under Article 161.
The ordinance-making power of the President (Article 123) and the Governor (Article 213) is non-discretionary and exercised on cabinet advice.
